reference: Independent getfacl CLI compares byte output, statuses and private file trees. Additional fixed POSIX mode-to-entry contracts and Bash metadata remain explicit contracts. Extended/default ACL fixtures are encoded independently from Linux POSIX ACL xattr version 2, using Python only for setup on relative paths.
coverage: Bash recognizes getfacl as a builtin and help exposes the documented synopsis and purpose.
Base access ACL entries are synthesized from two distinct ordinary file modes, including multiple path output.
Default header and --omit-header output using the runner-controlled relative filename and owner/group metadata.
--access and --omit-header aliases, plus -- termination for a relative filename beginning with a dash.
A missing operand among valid paths reports an error, preserves valid output, continues to later operands, and returns failure.
Missing operands and unknown options return usage errors.
Real GNU base/multiple/error comparisons plus independently seeded named access/default ACLs and effective-mask comments.
Default-only versus ordinary output from the same independently specified directory ACL.
exclusions: No real account or authentication configuration is changed; named ACL IDs are fixture-mapped and occur only in test-owned private file xattrs.
The harness tree snapshot does not record xattrs; getfacl output compares the decoded ACL text directly. Recursive traversal, broader NSS resolution and unrelated GNU flags remain outside this suite.
Arbitrary unmapped numeric ACL IDs need a disposable VM with the required ID mappings; the present user namespace accepts only mapped fixture IDs.
The case count exceeds the preferred range to retain original coverage and isolate independent additional edge cases.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash exposes the command as a builtin and that its help contains the documented synopsis and description.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help getfacl)
if [[ $(type -t getfacl) == builtin && $help_text == *'getfacl [-a] [-d] [--omit-header] file...'* && $help_text == *'Display POSIX.1e file access control lists.'* ]]; then
  printf 'builtin synopsis and help present\n'
else
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Check the documented base ACL synthesis for ordinary files with modes 0640 and 0600, and that multiple operands produce one separated ACL block each.
cases.script:
umask 027
: > readable
umask 077
: > private
getfacl -c readable private
cases.stdout:
user::rw-
group::r--
other::---

user::rw-
group::---
other::---

cases.purpose: Check the documented default file/owner/group header and its suppression with --omit-header. The harness maps the fixture's UID and GID to runner in its isolated passwd/group files.
cases.script:
umask 077
: > record
getfacl record
getfacl --omit-header record
cases.stdout:
# file: record
# owner: runner
# group: runner
user::rw-
group::---
other::---

user::rw-
group::---
other::---

cases.purpose: Check the documented --access and --omit-header aliases and the -- option terminator with a relative operand whose name starts with a dash.
Check multi-path error handling: a missing middle path emits a diagnostic while valid paths before and after it still produce their ACL blocks, and the overall status is failure.
cases.script:
umask 027
: > before
umask 077
: > after
getfacl -c before absent after
cases.stdout:
user::rw-
group::r--
other::---

user::rw-
group::---
other::---

cases.purpose: Check that invoking getfacl without any file operands is rejected as a usage error.
Check that an unrecognized option is rejected with a usage error and diagnostic.
Independently encode named access entries using the fixture-mapped UID/GID and a non-restrictive mask on a private file; compare GNU labels, ordering and mask output.
cases.script:
: > item
command -p python3 - <<'PYACL'
import os,struct
entries=[(1, 6, 4294967295), (2, 4, os.getuid()), (4, 4, 4294967295), (8, 4, os.getgid()), (16, 4, 4294967295), (32, 0, 4294967295)]
value=struct.pack('<I',2)+b''.join(struct.pack('<HHI',*entry) for entry in entries)
os.setxattr('item','system.posix_acl_access',value)
PYACL
getfacl -c item

cases.purpose: Independently seed a private directory default ACL and compare GNU default-only output, labels and ordering. GNU -d suppresses default: prefixes in this mode.
cases.script:
mkdir directory
command -p python3 - <<'PYACL'
import os,struct
entries=[(1, 6, 4294967295), (2, 4, os.getuid()), (4, 4, 4294967295), (8, 4, os.getgid()), (16, 4, 4294967295), (32, 0, 4294967295)]
value=struct.pack('<I',2)+b''.join(struct.pack('<HHI',*entry) for entry in entries)
os.setxattr('directory','system.posix_acl_default',value)
PYACL
getfacl -d directory

mkdir directory
chmod 751 directory
: > zero
chmod 000 zero
getfacl -c directory zero
chmod 600 zero
cases.stdout:
user::rwx
group::r-x
other::--x

user::---
group::---
other::---
